Penalized Likelihood Inference for Firth Logistic Regression

Source: R/logitFirth.R
logitFirth.Rd

Term-wise penalized likelihood ratio tests and profile penalized likelihood confidence intervals for logistic models fitted with fitMod(..., engine = "logitFirth").

Usage

# S3 method for class 'logitFirth'
drop1(object, scope, test = c("Chisq", "none"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'logitFirth'
confint(object, parm, level = 0.95, ...)

Arguments

object

a model fitted with fitMod(..., engine = "logitFirth")

scope

the terms to be tested, by default all terms that can be dropped, see drop1()

test

"Chisq" (default) for the penalized likelihood ratio test, "none" for the statistics only

...

further arguments, ignored

parm

the coefficients to compute intervals for, as names or indices. Default all.

level

the confidence level. Default 0.95.

Value

drop1() returns an object of class "anova" with the columns Df, PLR (the penalized likelihood ratio statistic) and, for test = "Chisq", Pr(>Chi). confint() returns a matrix with one row per coefficient and the lower and upper bound in its columns.

Details

Firth's method maximizes the penalized log-likelihood \(l^*(\beta) = l(\beta) + \frac{1}{2}\log|I(\beta)|\). Inference follows the penalized likelihood as well (Heinze and Schemper, 2002): the test statistic of a term is \(2\,(l^*(\hat\beta) - l^*(\hat\beta_0))\), where \(\hat\beta_0\) maximizes \(l^*\) with the coefficients of the term fixed at 0, and is referred to a chi-square distribution with as many degrees of freedom as the term has coefficients. A confidence interval collects all values of a coefficient that such a test would not reject.

The restricted fits keep the penalty of the full model. A refit without the columns of the term, as in brglm2:::drop1.brglmFit, changes the penalty and compares unpenalized deviances instead; the Wald intervals of brglm2:::confint.brglmFit are unreliable near separation, the situation Firth's method is used for.

The methods apply to the Jeffreys penalty with the logit link (type = "MPL_Jeffreys", the default of the engine, or the equivalent "AS_mean" and "AS_mixed" in brglm2::brglmFit). For other types the methods of brglm2 are used.

A bound that cannot be found within a wide search range (the profile does not reach the critical value) is returned as -Inf or Inf with a warning.

References

Firth, D. (1993) Bias reduction of maximum likelihood estimates. Biometrika 80, 27-38.

Heinze, G. and Schemper, M. (2002) A solution to the problem of separation in logistic regression. Statistics in Medicine 21, 2409-2419.

See also

Other modelling: classification-metrics, fitMod(), plot.FitMod(), predict.FitMod(), predictors(), print.FitMod(), regression-metrics

Examples

if (requireNamespace("brglm2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  fit <- fitMod(admit ~ gre + gpa + rank, Admit, engine = "logitFirth")
  drop1(fit)
  confint(fit)
}
#>                     2.5 %       97.5 %
#> (Intercept) -6.1654650411 -1.733021721
#> gre          0.0001124749  0.004365933
#> gpa          0.1504196393  1.440833495
#> rank2       -1.2847644285 -0.053262453
#> rank3       -1.9975621774 -0.655065307
#> rank4       -2.3448074019 -0.725328933
